headline: Singularity-Bench reports frontier agents building systems across six AI-development tasks
summary: The authors introduce Singularity-Bench, six open-ended tasks covering language-model pre-training, mid-training, post-training, inference, coding-agent harnesses and cluster orchestration. Each task has a bounded time and hardware budget and compares an agent-built system with a human-built reference. Across 11 configurations of seven models and two harnesses, the paper reports that Opus 5.5 with Claude Code beats five of six baselines and is statistically on par with the post-training reference, yielding a 1.252 average index relative to those references. This is an author-reported result from one benchmark; task scores, API spend and harness choice vary substantially. The authors say the tasks are still much smaller than full recursive self-improvement and leave substantial headroom.
